source.text: Καὶ ὑμᾶς ὄντας νεκροὺς τοῖς παραπτώμασιν καὶ ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν, ἐν αἷς ποτε περιεπατήσατε κατὰ τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, κατὰ τὸν ἄρχοντα τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ ἀέρος, τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ νῦν ἐνεργοῦντος ἐν τοῖς υἱοῖς τῆς ἀπειθείας·

records.literal_gloss: And you being dead in the trespasses and the sins of you, \v 2 in which once you walked according to the age of the world this, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit the [one] now working in the sons of the disobedience;

en.L: And you, being dead in your trespasses and sins, \v 2 in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit that is now working in the {{gender:children|sons}} of disobedience;
en.B: As for you, you were dead in your trespasses and sins. \v 2 You once lived in them, following the way of this world in its present age and following the ruler of the realm of the air, the ruler of the spirit now at work in those who disobey.
en.R: Once you were spiritually dead because of the wrong things you did and the sins you committed. \v 2 That is how you used to live. You followed the ways of this world as it is now. You obeyed the devil, who rules the realm of the air. He is the ruler of the spirit that is now at work in people who refuse to obey God.

es.L: Y a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, estando muertos en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} delitos y pecados, \v 2 en los cuales {{plural_you:anduvieron|anduvisteis}} en otro tiempo conforme a la era de este mundo, conforme al gobernante de la autoridad del aire, del espíritu que ahora actúa en los hijos de la desobediencia;
es.B: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} muertos en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} delitos y pecados. \v 2 En ellos {{plural_you:vivían|vivíais}} en otro tiempo, siguiendo el camino de este mundo en su era presente y siguiendo al gobernante del dominio del aire, el que gobierna también el espíritu que ahora actúa en los que desobedecen.
es.R: Antes {{plural_you:ustedes estaban|vosotros estabais}} muertos espiritualmente a causa del mal que {{plural_you:hacían|hacíais}} y de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pecados. \v 2 Así {{plural_you:vivían|vivíais}}. {{plural_you:Seguían|Seguíais}} los caminos de este mundo tal como es ahora. {{plural_you:Obedecían|Obedecíais}} al diablo, que gobierna el dominio del aire. Él gobierna el espíritu que ahora actúa en la gente que se niega a obedecer a Dios.

sw.L: Nanyi, mkiwa wafu katika makosa yenu na dhambi zenu, \v 2 ambazo ndani yake mlienenda zamani kufuatana na enzi ya ulimwengu huu, kufuatana na mtawala wa mamlaka ya anga, wa roho inayofanya kazi sasa ndani ya wana wa kutotii;
sw.B: Ninyi mlikuwa wafu katika makosa yenu na dhambi zenu. \v 2 Zamani mliishi katika mambo hayo, mkifuata njia ya ulimwengu huu katika enzi hii ya sasa, na mkimfuata mtawala wa milki ya anga, anayetawala pia roho ile inayofanya kazi sasa ndani ya wale wasiotii.
sw.R: Zamani mlikuwa wafu kiroho kwa sababu ya mabaya mliyotenda na dhambi mlizofanya. \v 2 Ndivyo mlivyoishi zamani. Mlifuata njia za ulimwengu huu kama ulivyo sasa. Mlimtii Shetani, anayetawala milki ya anga. Yeye ndiye mtawala wa roho ile inayofanya kazi sasa ndani ya watu wanaokataa kumtii Mungu.

fr.L: Et vous, étant morts dans vos fautes et vos péchés, \v 2 dans lesquels vous avez marché autrefois selon l’âge de ce monde, selon le prince de l’autorité de l’air, de l’esprit qui opère maintenant dans les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de la désobéissance ;
fr.B: Quant à vous, vous étiez morts dans vos fautes et vos péchés. \v 2 C’est en eux que vous avez vécu autrefois, en suivant les façons de ce monde dans le temps présent et en suivant le chef qui domine le royaume de l’air, le chef de l’esprit qui agit maintenant en ceux qui désobéissent.
fr.R: Autrefois, vous étiez morts spirituellement à cause du mal que vous faisiez et des péchés que vous commettiez. \v 2 C’est ainsi que vous viviez. Vous suiviez les façons de vivre de ce monde tel qu’il est aujourd’hui. Vous obéissiez au diable, qui domine le royaume de l’air. C’est lui qui commande l’esprit qui agit maintenant chez les gens qui refusent d’obéir à Dieu.

decisions.choice: the opening "you" waits for its verb: Paul breaks off and takes the sentence up again in verse 5, where God "made us alive together with Christ"
alternatives: supply "he made alive" here from verse 5
decisions.reason: ὑμᾶς is the object of a verb that never comes in verses 1-3. Paul describes what his readers were (verses 1-2) and what all believers were (verse 3), then starts again with ὁ δὲ θεὸς ("but God", verse 4), and the verb arrives in verse 5 with "us" in place of "you". The break makes the contrast sharp: dead, but God made alive. The record follows the SBLGNT, which ends the sentence at verse 2.

decisions.choice: dead in trespasses and sins: cut off from the life of God because of wrongdoing, and living in it
decisions.reason: They were alive in the ordinary sense, since they "walked" in these sins (verse 2). νεκροὺς means they had no share in God's life (4:18; Colossians 2:13), and could not give themselves life; only God could (verse 5). παραπτώμασιν (false steps) and ἁμαρτίαις (sins, missing the mark) are two words for the same thing, all their wrongdoing. The dative says both why they were dead and the condition they lived in.

decisions.choice: walked: lived, conducted their lives
decisions.reason: περιεπατήσατε ("you walked") is a Hebrew way of speaking of how a person lives (Psalm 1:1). Paul ends this passage with the same verb: believers are to walk in good works (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the age of this world: the world as it is in the present age, with its values and ways, set against God
alternatives: a personal spiritual power named Aeon
decisions.reason: αἰῶνα normally means an age or era. Paul speaks of "this age" as the present time that opposes God (Romans 12:2; Galatians 1:4), and of "the god of this age" (2 Corinthians 4:4). The word was later used for spiritual beings, but here it stands beside κόσμου ("world") and names a way of life, which the next phrase then traces to a personal ruler.

decisions.choice: the ruler of the authority of the air: the devil, ruling the realm where evil spiritual powers are at work
decisions.reason: ἄρχοντα is a ruler; the letter later names the devil and the spiritual forces of evil "in the heavenly places" as the believer's real enemy (6:11-12). Jesus calls him "the ruler of this world" (John 12:31). ἐξουσίας here is the domain where his authority runs, and may include the powers under him.

decisions.choice: the air: the region between the earth and the heavens
alternatives: the atmosphere in a merely physical sense
decisions.reason: ἀέρος is the air around and above the earth, below the heavens. In Jewish and other writing of the time this lower sky was often pictured as the place where evil spirits were active. Paul uses the picture to say that this ruler's power is near and real, not far away.

decisions.choice: the spirit now at work in the disobedient is something the ruler rules: a power and influence that works in people, under his control
alternatives: the spirit is the ruler himself, named a second way
the spirit is the same as "the authority of the air"
decisions.reason: τοῦ πνεύματος is genitive, like ἐξουσίας before it, so the easiest reading makes both depend on ἄρχοντα: he rules the realm of the air and also the spirit that works in disobedient people. If the spirit were the ruler himself, the case would be expected to match ἄρχοντα. The sense is close either way: the devil is behind the way they lived.

decisions.choice: the sons of disobedience: people whose lives are marked by disobedience to God
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 3:6 and Ephesians 5:6, "sons of" something is a Hebrew way of saying people characterized by it. It includes men and women. ἀπειθείας is refusal to obey God, which in the New Testament includes refusing to believe the gospel (Romans 11:30-32).

decisions.choice: As for you, you were dead
alternatives: And you, being dead (with the verb left until verse 5)
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the broken sentence a verb so that it can be read on its own; the main verb, "made alive", comes in verse 5 (m1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}} of disobedience
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 3:6, the phrase means people of either sex (m8); "sons" is the traditional form. Balanced and Readable say "those who disobey", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: spiritually dead because of the wrong things you did
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of death is meant (m2), and uses plainer words than "trespasses", as in Colossians 2:13.

decisions.choice: lived; used to live
decisions.reason: "Walked" for a way of life is an idiom (m3); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: You obeyed the devil, who rules the realm of the air ... people who refuse to obey God
alternatives: the ruler of the authority of the air
decisions.reason: Readable names the ruler (m5) and says who is disobeyed (m8).

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Paul writes to his readers in the plural throughout the chapter. Every plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in Philippians.

decisions.choice: hijos de la desobediencia, no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English offers "sons" as the traditional form. Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters, as in John 1:12, so the Spanish has no gender span here. Balanced and Readable say "los que desobedecen" and "la gente que se niega a obedecer", as the English does.

decisions.choice: wana wa kutotii, no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Wana" means children of either sex, so Swahili has no gender span where the English offers "sons" (docs/swahili-style.md 7). "Kutotii" (not obeying) is ἀπειθείας as refusing to obey God (m8); "uasi" (rebellion) says more.

decisions.choice: roho inayofanya kazi (class 9 agreement)
decisions.reason: The spirit here is a power under the ruler, not the ruler himself (m7). Swahili lets "roho" take either personal agreement (anayefanya) or the agreement of its noun class (inayofanya); the class 9 form keeps it a force at work in people and stops a reader taking it for the ruler or for God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: the settings, "passé composé" and the terms set out in chapter 1 hold for this chapter; les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de la désobéissance (L)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 3:6, "enfants" is the inclusive default for the Hebrew way of speaking of people marked by something (m8), with "fils" as the traditional form. Balanced and Readable say "ceux qui désobéissent", already inclusive. "Fautes" is used for the Greek word for false steps at Literal and Balanced, as in Colossians 2:13.

decisions.choice: vous avez marché (L), vous avez vécu (B, R); le prince (L), le chef (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of "walking" for a way of life (m3), which recurs through the letter (2:10, 4:1, 4:17, 5:2, 5:8, 5:15). "Prince" is the traditional French title for this ruler; Balanced says "chef", and Readable names him (m5).

source.text: ἐν οἷς καὶ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἀνεστράφημέν ποτε ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν, ποιοῦντες τὰ θελήματα τῆς σαρκὸς καὶ τῶν διανοιῶν, καὶ ἤμεθα τέκνα φύσει ὀργῆς ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί·

records.literal_gloss: among whom also we all lived once in the desires of the flesh of us, doing the wishes of the flesh and of the thoughts, and we were children by nature of wrath as also the rest;

en.L: among whom we also all once lived in the desires of our flesh, doing the wishes of the flesh and of the thoughts, and we were children of wrath by nature, as the rest also [were].
en.B: We all once lived among them too, following the desires of our flesh and doing whatever our flesh and our thoughts wanted. By nature we deserved God's wrath, just like the rest of humanity.
en.R: All of us used to live among those people too. We did whatever our sinful nature wanted. We followed its desires and the plans of our own minds. By our very nature we deserved God's anger, just like everyone else.

es.L: entre los cuales también todos nosotros nos conducíamos en otro tiempo en los deseos de nuestra carne, haciendo las voluntades de la carne y de los pensamientos, y éramos hijos de ira por naturaleza, como también los demás [lo eran].
es.B: También todos nosotros vivíamos antes entre ellos, siguiendo los deseos de nuestra carne y haciendo lo que querían nuestra carne y nuestros pensamientos. Por naturaleza merecíamos la ira de Dios, igual que el resto de la humanidad.
es.R: Todos nosotros también vivíamos antes entre esa gente. Hacíamos todo lo que quería nuestra naturaleza pecadora. Seguíamos sus deseos y los planes de nuestra propia mente. Por nuestra misma naturaleza merecíamos la ira de Dios, igual que todos los demás.

sw.L: miongoni mwa hao sisi pia sote tuliishi zamani katika tamaa za mwili wetu, tukifanya matakwa ya mwili na ya mawazo, na tulikuwa kwa asili watoto wa ghadhabu kama wengine nao [walivyokuwa].
sw.B: Sisi sote pia tuliishi zamani miongoni mwao, tukifuata tamaa za utu wetu wa dhambi na kufanya kila kitu ambacho utu huo na mawazo yetu vilitaka. Kwa asili tulistahili ghadhabu ya Mungu, sawa na wanadamu wengine wote.
sw.R: Sisi sote pia tuliishi zamani katikati ya watu hao. Tulifanya kila kitu ambacho utu wetu wa dhambi ulitaka. Tulifuata tamaa zake na mipango ya akili zetu wenyewe. Kwa asili yetu tulistahili ghadhabu ya Mungu, sawa na watu wengine wote.

fr.L: parmi lesquels nous aussi, nous tous, nous avons vécu autrefois dans les convoitises de notre chair, faisant les volontés de la chair et des pensées, et nous étions par nature des enfants de colère, comme les autres aussi.
fr.B: Nous tous aussi, nous avons vécu autrefois parmi eux, en suivant les désirs de notre chair et en faisant tout ce que voulaient notre chair et nos pensées. Par nature, nous méritions la colère de Dieu, comme le reste de l’humanité.
fr.R: Nous tous, nous vivions nous aussi parmi ces gens-là. Nous faisions tout ce que voulait notre nature pécheresse. Nous suivions ses désirs et les projets de notre propre esprit. Par notre nature même, nous méritions la colère de Dieu, comme tout le monde.

decisions.choice: among whom: among the disobedient people of verse 2
alternatives: in which: in the trespasses of verse 1
decisions.reason: οἷς can be masculine, pointing back to "the sons of disobedience", the nearest people named, or neuter, pointing to παραπτώμασιν. Verse 2 has already said "in which" of the sins, with a different pronoun (αἷς); here Paul says "we also" lived among the disobedient. Either way the point is the same: "we" shared that life.

decisions.choice: we all: Paul and his fellow Jewish believers, and with them all believers
decisions.reason: Paul turns from "you" (Gentile readers, verses 1-2) to "we". The emphatic ἡμεῖς πάντες ("we all") puts Jews and Gentiles in the same place: no one was an exception (Romans 3:9, 3:22-23). The same "we" continues into verses 4-7.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature turned away from God; the thoughts: the mind's own impulses
decisions.reason: σαρκὸς here is not the body as such but human life lived apart from God, with its desires (Galatians 5:16-21; Romans 8:5-8). διανοιῶν (plural, "thoughts") shows that the mind took part as well: not only bodily appetites but intentions and plans.

decisions.choice: children of wrath: people who deserve God's wrath and are under it
alternatives: people who are angry by temperament
decisions.reason: "Children of" something is a Hebrew way of speaking, like "sons of disobedience" in verse 2; in 1 Samuel 20:31 a "son of death" is a man who deserves to die. ὀργῆς is God's settled judgment against evil (5:6; Romans 1:18; Colossians 3:6), not a human mood.

decisions.choice: by nature: in what they were in themselves, not only in what they had done
decisions.reason: φύσει means by nature, as a thing is in itself (Galatians 2:15; 4:8). Paul says that apart from God's grace this was simply their condition. He does not say here when or how it began; Romans 5:12-19 is the place where he traces it back to Adam.

decisions.choice: the rest: the rest of humanity
decisions.reason: οἱ λοιποί are everyone else: Jews were in the same condition as Gentiles.

decisions.choice: we deserved God's wrath (B); we deserved God's anger (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m4) and name God, whose wrath it is. Readable says "anger" as Colossians 3:6 does, a plainer word.

decisions.choice: our sinful nature
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m3).

decisions.choice: la ira de Dios
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "anger" for a plainer word. Spanish "ira" is already an everyday word, so Spanish keeps the settled term at every level.

decisions.choice: utu wetu wa dhambi (our sinful self)
decisions.reason: Here "flesh" is human nature turned from God, not the body (m3), so Balanced and Readable do not say "mwili", which a reader would take as bodily appetite only. "Asili ya dhambi" (sinful nature) is the usual phrase, but the same verse says "kwa asili" (by nature) for φύσει, and using "asili" for both Greek words would blur them. Literal keeps "mwili".

decisions.choice: la chair (L, B); notre nature pécheresse (R)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 2:11-13, "chair" is kept at Literal and Balanced for human nature turned away from God (m3), so that the word can be followed; Readable says what it means.

source.text: ὁ δὲ θεὸς πλούσιος ὢν ἐν ἐλέει, διὰ τὴν πολλὴν ἀγάπην αὐτοῦ ἣν ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς, καὶ ὄντας ἡμᾶς νεκροὺς τοῖς παραπτώμασιν συνεζωοποίησεν τῷ Χριστῷ χάριτί ἐστε σεσῳσμένοι καὶ συνήγειρεν καὶ συνεκάθισεν ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα ἐνδείξηται ἐν τοῖς αἰῶσιν τοῖς ἐπερχομένοις τὸ ὑπερβάλλον πλοῦτος τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἐν χρηστότητι ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: But God rich being in mercy, because of the great love of him [with] which he loved us, \v 5 even being us dead in the trespasses, made alive together with the Christ — by grace you are saved — \v 6 and raised [us] together and seated [us] together in the heavenly [places] in Christ Jesus, \v 7 so that he might show in the ages the coming the surpassing riches of the grace of him in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.

en.L: But God, being rich in mercy, because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great love with which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved us, \v 5 even when we were dead in trespasses, made [us] alive together with the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (by grace you have been saved), \v 6 and raised [us] together and seated [us] together in the heavenly [places] in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, \v 7 in order that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might display in the ages that are coming the surpassing wealth of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace in kindness toward us in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.
en.B: But God is rich in mercy. Because of the great love {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had for us, \v 5 even when we were dead in our trespasses, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made us alive together with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. You have been saved by grace. \v 6 With {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} God raised us up, and with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} seated us in the heavenly places, in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, \v 7 so that through the ages still to come {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might put on display the wealth of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, which surpasses all measure, seen in the kindness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown us in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
en.R: But God's mercy is very great, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves us with a great love. \v 5 So even when we were spiritually dead because of our sins, God gave us life together with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. It is by God's grace that you have been saved! \v 6 God raised us up to life with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and gave us a place with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in heaven, because we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. \v 7 God did this so that for all time to come {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could show how very rich {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace is. He shows it by being kind to us in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

es.L: Pero Dios, siendo rico en misericordia, a causa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gran amor con el cual nos amó, \v 5 aun estando nosotros muertos en los delitos, [nos] vivificó juntamente con el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} (por gracia {{plural_you:han|habéis}} sido salvados), \v 6 y [nos] resucitó juntamente y [nos] sentó juntamente en los [lugares] celestiales en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|Mesías Jesús}}, \v 7 a fin de mostrar en las edades que vienen la riqueza sobreabundante de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia en bondad hacia nosotros en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|Mesías Jesús}}.
es.B: Pero Dios es rico en misericordia. Por el gran amor que nos tuvo, \v 5 aun cuando estábamos muertos en nuestros delitos, nos dio vida juntamente con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. Por gracia {{plural_you:ustedes han|vosotros habéis}} sido salvados. \v 6 Con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} Dios nos resucitó, y con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos sentó en los lugares celestiales, en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, \v 7 para exhibir en las edades que aún han de venir la riqueza de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, que sobrepasa toda medida, manifestada en la bondad que nos ha mostrado en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.
es.R: Pero la misericordia de Dios es muy grande, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos ama con un gran amor. \v 5 Por eso, aun cuando estábamos muertos espiritualmente a causa de nuestros pecados, Dios nos dio vida junto con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. ¡Es por la gracia de Dios que {{plural_you:ustedes han|vosotros habéis}} sido salvados! \v 6 Dios nos levantó a la vida con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} y nos dio un lugar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en el cielo, porque pertenecemos {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}. \v 7 Dios hizo esto para mostrar, por todos los tiempos que vendrán, lo inmensamente rica que es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia. Y la muestra al ser bondadoso con nosotros en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu, akiwa tajiri wa rehema, kwa sababu ya upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwingi ambao alitupenda nao, \v 5 hata tulipokuwa wafu katika makosa, alitufanya kuwa hai pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} (kwa neema mmeokolewa), \v 6 akatufufua pamoja [naye], akatuketisha pamoja [naye] katika [ulimwengu wa] mbinguni ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, \v 7 ili aonyeshe katika nyakati zinazokuja utajiri unaozidi mno wa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika wema kwetu ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.B: Lakini Mungu ni tajiri wa rehema. Kwa sababu ya upendo mkuu aliokuwa nao kwetu, \v 5 hata tulipokuwa wafu katika makosa yetu, alitufanya kuwa hai pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Mmeokolewa kwa neema. \v 6 Mungu alitufufua pamoja naye, na pamoja naye akatuketisha katika ulimwengu wa mbinguni, ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, \v 7 ili katika nyakati zote zijazo aonyeshe utajiri wa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, unaozidi kipimo chochote, unaoonekana katika wema aliotutendea ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.R: Lakini rehema ya Mungu ni kubwa sana, naye anatupenda kwa upendo mkuu. \v 5 Kwa hiyo hata tulipokuwa wafu kiroho kwa sababu ya dhambi zetu, Mungu alitupa uzima pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Ni kwa neema ya Mungu kwamba mmeokolewa! \v 6 Mungu alitufufua tuwe hai pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, akatupa nafasi pamoja naye mbinguni, kwa sababu sisi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. \v 7 Mungu alifanya hivyo ili kwa nyakati zote zijazo aonyeshe jinsi neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilivyo tajiri mno. Anaionyesha kwa kutufanyia wema ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.

fr.L: Mais Dieu, étant riche en miséricorde, à cause du grand amour dont {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a aimés, \v 5 alors même que nous étions morts dans les fautes, nous a rendus vivants avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (c’est par grâce que vous avez été sauvés), \v 6 et nous a ressuscités ensemble et fait asseoir ensemble dans les [lieux] célestes {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, \v 7 afin de montrer dans les âges qui viennent l’extraordinaire richesse de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, dans la bonté envers nous {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.B: Mais Dieu est riche en miséricorde. À cause du grand amour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a eu pour nous, \v 5 alors que nous étions morts dans nos fautes, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a rendus vivants avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. C’est par grâce que vous avez été sauvés. \v 6 Avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} Dieu nous a ressuscités, et avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} nous a fait asseoir dans les lieux célestes, {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, \v 7 afin de montrer, dans les âges à venir, la richesse de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, qui dépasse toute mesure, telle qu’on la voit dans la bonté qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a témoignée {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.R: Mais la miséricorde de Dieu est très grande, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous aime d’un grand amour. \v 5 Alors, même quand nous étions morts spirituellement à cause de nos péchés, Dieu nous a donné la vie avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. C’est par la grâce de Dieu que vous avez été sauvés ! \v 6 Dieu nous a ressuscités avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} pour une vie nouvelle, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a donné une place avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans le ciel, parce que nous appartenons au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. \v 7 Dieu l’a fait pour pouvoir montrer, pour toujours, combien {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce est riche. Il la montre en étant bon pour nous {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.

decisions.choice: Paul takes up the sentence he broke off in verse 1: God is the subject, and "made alive" is its main verb
decisions.reason: ὁ δὲ θεὸς ("but God") answers the "you" of verse 1, and verse 5 repeats "being dead in trespasses" from verse 1, now with "us". The three verbs that follow say what God has done.

decisions.choice: rich in mercy, out of great love: the reason for God's action lies in God, not in those he saved
decisions.reason: ἐλέει is pity that acts to help, and ἀγάπην ... ἠγάπησεν ("the love with which he loved") doubles the word for love. Paul gives no reason in the people themselves: they were dead (verse 5).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "made us alive together with Christ"
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts add ἐν ("in") before τῷ Χριστῷ, giving "in Christ", perhaps to match "in Christ Jesus" in verses 6-7. The SBLGNT follows the reading without it, where the dative goes with the "together" of the verb: alive together with Christ. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: by grace you have been saved: a short cry that breaks into the sentence, saying that their salvation is already done and still stands
decisions.reason: The perfect σεσῳσμένοι says the saving happened and its result remains. Paul breaks his sentence to say it, and turns from "us" back to "you". He comes back to the words in verse 8 and explains them.

decisions.choice: made alive with, raised with, seated with: what God did for Christ, God has done for believers joined to him
alternatives: Jews and Gentiles made alive together, with each other
decisions.reason: συνεζωοποίησεν, συνήγειρεν and συνεκάθισεν all begin with a prefix meaning "together with". God raised Christ from the dead and seated him in the heavenly places (1:20); now Paul says the same of believers, in Christ. He speaks of it as already done, because they are joined to Christ, though they still wait for its full outcome (1:14; Colossians 3:1-4). The first verb names Christ as the one they are joined with.

decisions.choice: the heavenly places: the heavenly realm where Christ now reigns
decisions.reason: As in 1:3 and 1:20, ἐπουρανίοις is the heavenly realm. Here it is the place where Christ sits at God's right hand (1:20), and believers are said to share his place there.

decisions.choice: the coming ages: all time to come, without end
alternatives: the generations still to come in this world's history
decisions.reason: αἰῶσιν τοῖς ἐπερχομένοις ("the ages coming") looks forward to all the future, as "this age and the one to come" does in 1:21. God's kindness to them will be on show for ever.

decisions.choice: in kindness toward us: the way God displays the wealth of his grace
decisions.reason: ἐν χρηστότητι says how the grace is seen: in God's kindness to people like those of verses 1-3, who deserved wrath.

decisions.choice: You have been saved by grace. (B); It is by God's grace that you have been saved! (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Paul's interjection (m4) its own short sentence, so that the long sentence can be read aloud.

decisions.choice: With {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} God raised us up, and with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} seated us (B); God raised us up to life with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and gave us a place with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the subject and say who the "together" is with (m5).

decisions.choice: in heaven
decisions.reason: As in the rest of Ephesians at this level, Readable uses the plain word (m6).

decisions.choice: because we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in Christ Jesus" means here: these things are true of believers because they are joined to Christ (m5).

decisions.choice: spiritually dead because of our sins
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on written pronouns
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject inside the verb ("nos amó", "nos sentó"), so the setting applies only where a pronoun is written ("su gracia", "con él"). The Spanish therefore has fewer pronoun spans than the English.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives
decisions.reason: Swahili marks the subject and object inside the verb (alitupenda, akatufufua) and joins "na" and "yeye" into "naye"; none of these can take a capital. The setting applies to free possessives such as "upendo wake" and "neema yake", so the Swahili has fewer spans than the English.

decisions.choice: ulimwengu wa mbinguni (L, B); mbinguni (R)
decisions.reason: Here the heavenly places are where Christ sits at God's right hand (m6), so Swahili names heaven itself rather than "ulimwengu wa roho" (the spirit world), which would also suit the realm of the evil powers in 6:12. Literal brackets "ulimwengu wa", which the Greek lacks.

decisions.choice: vous avez été sauvés (every level, here and in 2:8)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect says that the rescue has happened and its result stands (m4). "Vous êtes sauvés" would stress only the present state; "vous avez été sauvés" names the act, and in French its result is still understood.

source.text: τῇ γὰρ χάριτί ἐστε σεσῳσμένοι διὰ πίστεως· καὶ τοῦτο οὐκ ἐξ ὑμῶν, θεοῦ τὸ δῶρον·

records.literal_gloss: By the for grace you are saved through faith; and this not from you, of God the gift;

en.L: For by the grace you have been saved through faith; and this [is] not from you; of God [is] the gift;
en.B: For it is by this grace that you have been saved, through faith. None of this comes from you; it is God's gift.
en.R: You have been saved because of God's grace, and it came to you through faith. Being saved does not come from you. God gives it as a gift.

es.L: Porque por la gracia {{plural_you:han|habéis}} sido salvados por medio de [la] fe; y esto no [viene] de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, de Dios [es] el don;
es.B: Porque es por esta gracia que {{plural_you:ustedes han|vosotros habéis}} sido salvados, por medio de la fe. Nada de esto sale de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}: es don de Dios.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes han|Vosotros habéis}} sido salvados a causa de la gracia de Dios, y esa salvación {{plural_you:les|os}} llegó por medio de la fe. Ser salvos no viene de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Es un regalo de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa neema mmeokolewa kupitia imani; na hili si kutoka kwenu, zawadi [ni] ya Mungu;
sw.B: Kwa maana ni kwa neema hiyo mmeokolewa, kupitia imani. Jambo hili halitoki kwenu; ni zawadi ya Mungu.
sw.R: Mmeokolewa kwa sababu ya neema ya Mungu, na wokovu huo uliwafikia kupitia imani. Kuokolewa hakutoki kwenu. Mungu anautoa kama zawadi.

fr.L: Car c’est par la grâce que vous avez été sauvés, par la foi ; et cela [ne vient] pas de vous, [c’est] le don de Dieu ;
fr.B: Car c’est par cette grâce que vous avez été sauvés, par la foi. Rien de cela ne vient de vous : c’est le don de Dieu.
fr.R: Vous avez été sauvés par la grâce de Dieu, et cela vous est parvenu par la foi. Être sauvé, cela ne vient pas de vous. C’est un cadeau que Dieu vous fait.

decisions.choice: "this" is the whole of what Paul has just said: being saved by grace through faith
decisions.reason: τοῦτο is neuter, while χάριτί and πίστεως are both feminine. Paul often uses a neuter "this" for a whole statement rather than one word (Philippians 1:28). What follows fits salvation as a whole: it is "not from you", it is God's gift, and it is "not from works" (verse 9), which could not be said of faith on its own. Faith is part of what is given, but Paul's point is that the whole of salvation, from first to last, comes from God.

decisions.choice: by the grace: the grace just spoken of in verses 5 and 7
decisions.reason: τῇ has the article, pointing back to the grace of verse 5 ("by grace you have been saved") and the wealth of grace in verse 7. γὰρ ("for") explains why God's kindness will be on show: everything about their salvation is grace.

decisions.choice: through faith: faith is the way salvation is received, not its cause
decisions.reason: χάριτί (dative, "by grace") is the source of salvation; διὰ πίστεως ("through faith") is the channel by which it reaches people. Faith is trust in God and in Christ (1:13, 1:15).

decisions.choice: gift: something given freely, not earned
decisions.reason: δῶρον is a present. θεοῦ comes first in its clause for emphasis: God's is the gift, set against ἐξ ὑμῶν ("from you").

decisions.choice: None of this comes from you
decisions.reason: "This" after "through faith" would be read as "faith". "None of this" points to the whole statement, as the Greek does (m1); Literal keeps "this".

decisions.choice: Being saved does not come from you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this" refers to (m1).

decisions.choice: by this grace
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the article points back to the grace of verses 5-7 (m2).

decisions.choice: esto (neuter)
decisions.reason: Spanish has a neuter demonstrative, as Greek does here. "Esto" points to the whole statement, being saved by grace through faith (m1); "esta" would point to "la fe" or "la gracia" alone.

decisions.choice: hili / jambo hili
decisions.reason: "Hii" would agree with "neema" or "imani" (both class 9) and point to one of them. "Hili", the class 5 form used for a matter or affair ("jambo hili"), points to the whole statement, as the Greek neuter does (m1).

decisions.choice: Rien de cela (B)
decisions.reason: As in English: "cela" right after "par la foi" would be read as the faith alone; "rien de cela" points to the whole of being saved by grace through faith (m1). Literal keeps the plain "cela".

source.text: οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων, ἵνα μή τις καυχήσηται.

records.literal_gloss: not from works, so that not anyone may boast.

en.L: not from works, in order that no one might boast.
en.B: It is not the result of what anyone has done, so there is no room for anyone to boast.
en.R: Nobody earns it by the things they do, so nobody can boast about it.

es.L: no de obras, a fin de que nadie se jacte.
es.B: No es fruto de lo que alguien haya hecho; así nadie tiene de qué jactarse.
es.R: Nadie se la gana por las cosas que hace, así que nadie puede presumir de ella.

sw.L: si kutoka kwa matendo, ili mtu yeyote asijisifu.
sw.B: Halitokani na yale ambayo mtu yeyote ametenda, kwa hiyo hakuna nafasi ya mtu yeyote kujisifu.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu anayeupata wokovu kwa matendo yake, kwa hiyo hakuna anayeweza kujisifu kwa ajili yake.

fr.L: non pas des œuvres, afin que personne ne se vante.
fr.B: Cela ne vient pas de ce que quelqu’un a fait, et ainsi personne n’a de quoi se vanter.
fr.R: Personne ne le gagne par ce qu’il fait, et donc personne ne peut s’en vanter.

decisions.choice: "not from works" completes verse 8: it says again where salvation does not come from
decisions.reason: οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων matches οὐκ ἐξ ὑμῶν ("not from you") in verse 8. The SBLGNT ends verse 8 with a raised dot, so verse 9 stands as its own record, but it has no verb and continues the same thought.

decisions.choice: works: anything people do that might be thought to earn God's favor
alternatives: only the works required by the law of Moses
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Paul speaks of "works of the law" (Galatians 2:16; Romans 3:28). Here ἔργων has no qualifier and is addressed to Gentiles as well as Jews, so it covers human deeds of every kind. Verse 10 shows that good works still matter: they are the result of salvation, not its cause.

decisions.choice: so that no one may boast: God's purpose in saving this way
alternatives: with the result that no one can boast
decisions.reason: ἵνα states purpose: God saves by grace so that no one can take credit before him (1 Corinthians 1:29-31; Romans 3:27). καυχήσηται is boasting in the sense of claiming credit.

decisions.choice: It is not the result of what anyone has done (B); Nobody earns it by the things they do (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the phrase a subject and a verb so it can stand as a sentence (m1), and say what "works" means (m2).

source.text: αὐτοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν ποίημα, κτισθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἐπὶ ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς οἷς προητοίμασεν ὁ θεὸς ἵνα ἐν αὐτοῖς περιπατήσωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: Of him for we are [a] thing made, having been created in Christ Jesus for works good which prepared beforehand the God so that in them we might walk.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} handiwork we are, having been created in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus for good works that God prepared in advance, so that in them we might walk.
en.B: For we are God's own work. In {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} created us for good works, which God made ready in advance so that we would live our lives doing them.
en.R: God is the one who made us what we are. He created us new because we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, so that we would do good things. God got these good things ready ahead of time, so that we would live by doing them.

es.L: Porque de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} somos obra, habiendo sido creados en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|Mesías Jesús}} para obras buenas que Dios preparó con anticipación, a fin de que en ellas caminemos.
es.B: Porque somos obra del mismo Dios. En {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} nos creó para buenas obras, que Dios dispuso de antemano para que vivamos practicándolas.
es.R: Dios es quien nos hizo lo que somos. Nos creó de nuevo porque pertenecemos {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}, para que hagamos cosas buenas. Dios preparó esas cosas buenas desde antes, para que vivamos haciéndolas.

sw.L: Kwa maana sisi ni kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, tulioumbwa ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kwa ajili ya matendo mema ambayo Mungu aliyaandaa mapema ili tuenende katika hayo.
sw.B: Kwa maana sisi ni kazi ya Mungu mwenyewe. Ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu alituumba kwa ajili ya matendo mema, ambayo Mungu aliyaandaa mapema ili maisha yetu yawe ya kuyatenda.
sw.R: Mungu ndiye aliyetufanya tulivyo. Alituumba upya kwa sababu sisi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, ili tufanye mambo mema. Mungu aliyaandaa mambo hayo mema tangu zamani, ili tuishi kwa kuyatenda.

fr.L: Car nous sommes {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ouvrage, ayant été créés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus pour des œuvres bonnes que Dieu a préparées d’avance afin que nous marchions en elles.
fr.B: Car nous sommes l’ouvrage de Dieu. {{christos:En Christ|Dans le Messie}} Jésus, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a créés pour les œuvres bonnes que Dieu a préparées d’avance, afin que nous passions notre vie à les accomplir.
fr.R: C’est Dieu qui a fait de nous ce que nous sommes. Il nous a créés de nouveau parce que nous appartenons au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, pour que nous fassions le bien. Dieu a préparé d’avance ce bien à faire, pour que nous vivions en le faisant.

decisions.choice: a thing made: what God has made, here his new creation in Christ
alternatives: a masterpiece or work of art
decisions.reason: ποίημα is the ordinary word for something made, used of God's works in creation (Romans 1:20). The word "poem" comes from it, but in the Greek of the time it does not itself mean a work of art. The next word, κτισθέντες ("created"), shows what kind of making Paul means.

decisions.choice: his work: God's doing, not ours
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ stands first for emphasis, and γάρ ("for") ties the verse to verses 8-9: salvation is not from works, because we ourselves are God's work. The "his" is God, named as the giver in verse 8 and as the one who prepared the works in this verse.

decisions.choice: created in Christ Jesus: made new by being joined to Christ
decisions.reason: Paul uses the language of creation for what God does in salvation (2 Corinthians 5:17; Galatians 6:15). In verse 15 Christ "creates" one new humanity, and in 4:24 the new self is "created" to be like God.

decisions.choice: for good works, which God prepared beforehand for us to walk in: good works are the purpose of the new creation, not its cause
alternatives: God prepared the people beforehand for good works
decisions.reason: ἐπὶ ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς gives the goal. οἷς ("which") refers to the works: God prepared them in advance, and believers are to walk in them. περιπατήσωμεν ("we might walk") takes up the word of verse 2: the life once lived in sins is now to be lived in good works.

decisions.choice: God's own work (B); God is the one who made us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God (m2), and keep the emphasis on God as the maker.

decisions.choice: God's own work (B); made us what we are (R)
decisions.reason: The word means something made (m1). "Masterpiece" says more than the Greek does, and "workmanship" is no longer everyday English.

decisions.choice: live our lives doing them (B); live by doing them (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" is an idiom for a way of life (verse 2, m3); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: He created us new because we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says that this creation is a new one, and what "in Christ" means (m3).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ouvrage (L); l’ouvrage de Dieu (B)
decisions.reason: The word means a thing made (m1). "Chef-d’œuvre" says more than the Greek, and "ouvrage" keeps "œuvre" free for the "works" of verses 9-10, so the reader can see that God’s making comes before our works (m4).

source.text: Διὸ μνημονεύετε ὅτι ποτὲ ὑμεῖς τὰ ἔθνη ἐν σαρκί, οἱ λεγόμενοι ἀκροβυστία ὑπὸ τῆς λεγομένης περιτομῆς ἐν σαρκὶ χειροποιήτου, ὅτι ἦτε τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ χωρὶς Χριστοῦ, ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι τῆς πολιτείας τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ξένοι τῶν διαθηκῶν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, ἐλπίδα μὴ ἔχοντες καὶ ἄθεοι ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore remember that once you the Gentiles in flesh, the [ones] being called uncircumcision by the [one] being called circumcision in flesh made by hands, \v 12 that you were at the time that without Christ, having been alienated from the citizenship of the Israel and strangers of the covenants of the promise, hope not having and without God in the world.

en.L: Therefore remember that once you, the Gentiles in [the] flesh, who are called "uncircumcision" by what is called "circumcision", in [the] flesh, made by hands— \v 12 that at that time you were without {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, excluded from the citizenship of Israel and strangers to the covenants of the promise, not having hope, and without God in the world.
en.B: So remember what you once were: Gentiles by birth, labeled "the uncircumcised" by those who are called "the circumcised", a circumcision performed on the body by human hands. \v 12 Remember that at that time you were without {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. You were excluded from citizenship in Israel and were strangers to the covenants built on God's promise. You had no hope, and you were without God in the world.
en.R: So remember what you were before. You were Gentiles, people who are not Jewish by birth. Jewish people called you "the uncircumcised," and they called themselves "the circumcised." (Circumcision is a cut made in the body by human hands. It was the sign that a man belonged to God's people, Israel.) \v 12 Remember that back then you did not have {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. You were not part of Israel, the people of God. You had no share in the covenants, the agreements God made with Israel, or in the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave in them. You had no hope, and you lived in the world without God.

es.L: Por tanto, {{plural_you:recuerden|recordad}} que en otro tiempo {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los gentiles en [la] carne, los llamados «incircuncisión» por la llamada «circuncisión» en [la] carne, hecha a mano— \v 12 que en aquel tiempo {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} sin {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, excluidos de la ciudadanía de Israel y extranjeros a los pactos de la promesa, sin tener esperanza y sin Dios en el mundo.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:recuerden|recordad}} lo que {{plural_you:ustedes eran|vosotros erais}} antes: gentiles de nacimiento, a quienes llamaban «los incircuncisos» aquellos que se llaman «los circuncisos», por una circuncisión hecha en el cuerpo por manos humanas. \v 12 {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} que en aquel tiempo {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} sin {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. {{plural_you:Estaban|Estabais}} excluidos de la ciudadanía de Israel y {{plural_you:eran|erais}} extranjeros en cuanto a los pactos basados en la promesa de Dios. No {{plural_you:tenían|teníais}} esperanza, y {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} sin Dios en el mundo.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:recuerden|recordad}} lo que {{plural_you:eran|erais}} antes. {{plural_you:Eran|Erais}} gentiles, es decir, personas que no son judías de nacimiento. Los judíos {{plural_you:los|os}} llamaban «los incircuncisos», y a sí mismos se llamaban «los circuncisos». (La circuncisión es un corte hecho en el cuerpo por manos humanas. Era la señal de que un hombre pertenecía al pueblo de Dios, Israel). \v 12 {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} que en aquel tiempo no {{plural_you:tenían|teníais}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. No {{plural_you:formaban|formabais}} parte de Israel, el pueblo de Dios. No {{plural_you:tenían|teníais}} parte en los pactos, los acuerdos que Dios hizo con Israel, ni en la promesa que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dio en ellos. No {{plural_you:tenían|teníais}} esperanza, y {{plural_you:vivían|vivíais}} en el mundo sin Dios.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo kumbukeni kwamba zamani ninyi, watu wa mataifa katika mwili, mnaoitwa "Kutotahiriwa" na ile inayoitwa "Tohara" katika mwili, iliyofanywa kwa mikono— \v 12 kwamba wakati ule mlikuwa bila {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, mkiwa mmetengwa na uraia wa Israeli na wageni kuhusu maagano ya ahadi, bila kuwa na tumaini, na bila Mungu ulimwenguni.
sw.B: Basi kumbukeni mlivyokuwa zamani: watu wa mataifa kwa kuzaliwa, mlioitwa "wasiotahiriwa" na wale wanaoitwa "waliotahiriwa", kwa sababu ya tohara inayofanywa mwilini kwa mikono ya wanadamu. \v 12 Kumbukeni kwamba wakati ule mlikuwa bila {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Mlikuwa mmetengwa na uraia wa Israeli, na mlikuwa wageni kuhusu maagano yaliyojengwa juu ya ahadi ya Mungu. Hamkuwa na tumaini, na mlikuwa bila Mungu ulimwenguni.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kumbukeni mlivyokuwa zamani. Mlikuwa watu wasio Wayahudi kwa kuzaliwa. Wayahudi waliwaita "wasiotahiriwa," nao wakajiita "waliotahiriwa." (Tohara ni kukata sehemu ya mwili kwa mikono ya wanadamu. Ilikuwa ishara kwamba mwanamume ni wa watu wa Mungu, Israeli.) \v 12 Kumbukeni kwamba wakati ule hamkuwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Hamkuwa sehemu ya Israeli, watu wa Mungu. Hamkuwa na sehemu katika maagano, yaani mapatano ambayo Mungu alifanya na Israeli, wala katika ahadi aliyotoa ndani yake. Hamkuwa na tumaini, na mliishi ulimwenguni bila Mungu.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi souvenez-vous qu’autrefois vous, les nations dans la chair, appelés « incirconcision » par ce qu’on appelle « circoncision », dans la chair, faite par des mains, \v 12 qu’en ce temps-là vous étiez sans {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, exclus de la cité d’Israël et étrangers aux alliances de la promesse, n’ayant pas d’espérance et sans Dieu dans le monde.
fr.B: Souvenez-vous donc de ce que vous étiez autrefois : vous qui, par votre naissance, n’étiez pas juifs, vous étiez appelés « les incirconcis » par ceux qu’on appelle « les circoncis », d’une circoncision faite dans le corps par des mains humaines. \v 12 Souvenez-vous qu’en ce temps-là vous étiez sans le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Vous étiez privés du droit de cité en Israël et étrangers aux alliances fondées sur la promesse de Dieu. Vous n’aviez pas d’espérance, et vous étiez sans Dieu dans le monde.
fr.R: Souvenez-vous donc de ce que vous étiez avant. Vous n’étiez pas juifs de naissance. Les Juifs vous appelaient « les incirconcis », et ils s’appelaient eux-mêmes « les circoncis ». (La circoncision est une coupure faite dans le corps par des mains humaines. C’était le signe qu’un homme appartenait au peuple de Dieu, Israël.) \v 12 Souvenez-vous qu’à cette époque, vous n’aviez pas le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Vous ne faisiez pas partie d’Israël, le peuple de Dieu. Vous n’aviez aucune part aux alliances, les accords que Dieu avait faits avec Israël, ni à la promesse qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y avait donnée. Vous n’aviez pas d’espérance, et vous viviez dans le monde sans Dieu.

decisions.choice: Paul begins "remember that", breaks off to describe the labels, and starts again with a second "that" in verse 12
decisions.reason: The first ὅτι (verse 11) is followed by a description of how the readers were named; the second ὅτι (verse 12) gives what they are to remember. Both clauses depend on μνημονεύετε ("remember").

decisions.choice: the Gentiles in the flesh: Gentiles by birth and in their bodies
decisions.reason: ἐν σαρκί here is physical: they were not Jews by descent and did not bear the bodily mark of circumcision. It is not the moral sense of "flesh" in verse 3.

decisions.choice: uncircumcision and circumcision were labels: Jews called Gentiles "the uncircumcision", and were themselves called "the circumcision"
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham and his descendants (Genesis 17:9-14), so Jews could name Gentiles by its absence, often with contempt (1 Samuel 17:26), and Jews were known as "the circumcision" (Galatians 2:7-9). λεγόμενοι and λεγομένης ("called") show that Paul is reporting names others used. He holds that the outward mark is not what counts before God (Galatians 6:15; Colossians 2:11).

decisions.choice: made by hands: a human act, as against what God does
decisions.reason: χειροποιήτου describes what is merely human work. Elsewhere it is set against what God makes: the temple "made with hands" (Mark 14:58; Acts 7:48) and the circumcision "made without hands" that Christ gives (Colossians 2:11).

decisions.choice: without Christ: with no part in the Messiah whom God had promised to Israel
decisions.reason: χωρὶς Χριστοῦ heads a list of what Israel had and the Gentiles did not. Israel's hope looked toward the promised Messiah (Romans 9:4-5); the Gentiles had no share in that hope.

decisions.choice: excluded from the citizenship of Israel: shut out from belonging to Israel as God's people
alternatives: cut off from Israel's way of life
decisions.reason: ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι means shut out, made strangers (4:18; Colossians 1:21). πολιτείας is a citizen body and the rights of belonging to it; Israel is pictured as a commonwealth to which Gentiles had no claim. Verse 19 answers this: they are now "fellow citizens".

decisions.choice: the covenants of the promise: God's covenants with Abraham, Israel and David, all bound up with his promise
decisions.reason: διαθηκῶν is plural. God made covenants with Abraham (Genesis 15; 17), with Israel at Sinai (Exodus 24), and with David (2 Samuel 7), and promised a new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31-34). Romans 9:4 lists "the covenants" and "the promises" among Israel's gifts. The promise is God's promise to bless all nations through Abraham's offspring (Galatians 3:16-18).

decisions.choice: without God: not knowing the true God
alternatives: atheists, denying that any god exists
decisions.reason: ἄθεοι does not mean they believed in no god; they had many gods (1 Corinthians 8:5). They did not know the God of Israel (Galatians 4:8; 1 Thessalonians 4:5), and so were without God in the world.

decisions.choice: "the uncircumcised"; "the circumcised"
decisions.reason: The labels name groups of people (m3); Balanced and Readable use the English forms for people. Literal keeps the Greek nouns.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jewish by birth ... (Circumcision is a cut made in the body by human hands. It was the sign that a man belonged to God's people, Israel.)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles" on its first use in the chapter, and what circumcision was, so that the labels make sense (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: excluded from citizenship in Israel
alternatives: alienated from the commonwealth of Israel
decisions.reason: "Citizenship" prepares for "fellow citizens" in verse 19 (m6).

decisions.choice: the covenants, the agreements God made with Israel, or ... the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave in them
alternatives: strangers to the covenants of the promise
decisions.reason: Readable says what the covenants were and whose promise it was (m7).

decisions.choice: you did not have {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: A plain way of saying they had no part in the Messiah (m5).

decisions.choice: "Kutotahiriwa" and "Tohara" (L); "wasiotahiriwa", "waliotahiriwa" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek labels as nouns for a condition, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable name the groups of people (m3). "Tohara" is the noun for the rite, so "ile inayoitwa" and "iliyofanywa" agree with it.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); vous qui, par votre naissance, n’étiez pas juifs (B); vous n’étiez pas juifs de naissance (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 1:27: "les Gentils" is no longer current French, and "les païens" now suggests people with no religion, or a judgment. Literal keeps "les nations", the biblical name for the peoples other than Israel; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m2). "Non-Juifs" is used where a short noun is needed (2:17-18, 3:1).

decisions.choice: privés du droit de cité en Israël (B)
decisions.reason: "Droit de cité" is the French for a citizen’s rights, and it prepares for "concitoyens" in verse 19 (m6).

source.text: νυνὶ δὲ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ὑμεῖς οἵ ποτε ὄντες μακρὰν ἐγενήθητε ἐγγὺς ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Now but in Christ Jesus you the [ones] once being far off became near by the blood of the Christ.

en.L: But now in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus you who once were far away became near by the blood of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: But now you who were once far away are in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, and the blood of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has brought you near.
en.R: But now you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. You were once far away from God and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, but now you have come near. It happened through the blood {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} shed when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died on the cross.

es.L: Pero ahora en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|Mesías Jesús}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que en otro tiempo {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} lejos, {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a estar cerca por la sangre del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.B: Pero ahora {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que antes {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} lejos, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, y por la sangre {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} {{plural_you:han|habéis}} sido traídos cerca.
es.R: Pero ahora {{plural_you:ustedes pertenecen|vosotros pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}. Antes {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} lejos de Dios y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, pero ahora {{plural_you:se han|os habéis}} acercado. Esto sucedió por medio de la sangre que {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} derramó cuando murió en la cruz.

sw.L: Lakini sasa ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu ninyi ambao zamani mlikuwa mbali mlifanyika [kuwa] karibu kwa damu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Lakini sasa ninyi mliokuwa mbali zamani mko ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, na damu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} imewaleta karibu.
sw.R: Lakini sasa ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Zamani mlikuwa mbali na Mungu na watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, lakini sasa mmekaribia. Hilo lilitokea kupitia damu ambayo {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alimwaga alipokufa msalabani.

fr.L: Mais maintenant, {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, vous qui autrefois étiez loin, vous êtes devenus proches par le sang du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Mais maintenant, vous qui étiez autrefois loin, vous êtes {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, et le sang du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} vous a rapprochés.
fr.R: Mais maintenant, vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. Autrefois, vous étiez loin de Dieu et de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple, mais maintenant vous êtes tout près. Cela s’est fait par le sang que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} a versé quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort sur la croix.

decisions.choice: far and near: Isaiah's words, which Paul quotes in verse 17
decisions.reason: Isaiah 57:19 announces "peace to the far and to the near". Israel was described as a people "near" to God (Psalm 148:14), and Gentiles as "far off" (Acts 2:39). Far from God and from his people (verse 12), the Gentiles have been brought near to both.

decisions.choice: the blood of Christ: his death as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: αἵματι stands for Christ's death, given as a sacrifice, as in 1:7 ("redemption through his blood") and Colossians 1:20 ("the blood of his cross"). Verse 16 names the cross.

decisions.choice: but now ... once: the turn from their past to their present
decisions.reason: νυνὶ δὲ ("but now") answers ποτε ("once") here and in verse 11, as "but God" answered verses 1-3. ἐγενήθητε is passive in form but means "became"; Christ's blood is the means by which the change came about.

decisions.choice: far away from God and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people ... come near
decisions.reason: Readable says what they were far from (m1).

decisions.choice: the blood {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} shed when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died on the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the blood" stands for (m2).

decisions.choice: you who were once far away are in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, and the blood of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has brought you near
alternatives: in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus you who once were far away have come near by the blood of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Balanced splits the sentence into two clauses to keep the two phrases about Christ apart.

source.text: αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ ἀμφότερα ἓν καὶ τὸ μεσότοιχον τοῦ φραγμοῦ λύσας, τὴν ἔχθραν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ, τὸν νόμον τῶν ἐντολῶν ἐν δόγμασιν καταργήσας, ἵνα τοὺς δύο κτίσῃ ἐν αὑτῷ εἰς ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον ποιῶν εἰρήνην, καὶ ἀποκαταλλάξῃ τοὺς ἀμφοτέρους ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ σταυροῦ ἀποκτείνας τὴν ἔχθραν ἐν αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: He himself for is the peace of us, the [one] having made the both one and the dividing wall of the fence having broken down, the hostility, in the flesh of him, \v 15 the law of the commandments in decrees having abolished, so that the two he might create in himself into one new man, making peace, \v 16 and might reconcile the both in one body to the God through the cross, having killed the hostility in it;

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is our peace, who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of the barrier, the hostility, in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flesh, \v 15 having abolished the law of the commandments in decrees, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might create the two in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} into one new {{gender:human being|man}}, making peace, \v 16 and might reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the hostility by it;
en.B: For {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is our peace. He has made the two groups into one, and has broken down the wall that divided them, the hostility between them. In {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body \v 15 {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set aside the law with its commandments and regulations. He did this to create in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} one new humanity out of the two, so making peace, \v 16 and to reconcile both of them to God in one body through the cross, by which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put the hostility to death.
en.R: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is our peace. He has made Jews and Gentiles into one people. A wall stood between them, and they were like enemies. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the wall down when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body. \v 15 He ended the power of the law, with all its commands and rules, to keep them apart. He did this to make the two groups into one new people, joined to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. In this way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made peace. \v 16 Through the cross {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought both groups to God as one body, at peace with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. On the cross {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put an end to the hostility.

es.L: Porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo es nuestra paz, el que hizo de ambos uno y derribó la pared intermedia de la separación, la enemistad, en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} carne, \v 15 habiendo anulado la ley de los mandamientos en decretos, para crear en {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} de los dos un solo {{gender:ser humano|hombre}} nuevo, haciendo la paz, \v 16 y reconciliar con Dios a ambos en un solo cuerpo por medio de la cruz, habiendo dado muerte a la enemistad por ella;
es.B: Porque {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} mismo es nuestra paz. Ha hecho de los dos grupos uno solo, y ha derribado el muro que los dividía, la enemistad que había entre ellos. En {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio cuerpo \v 15 dejó sin efecto la ley con sus mandamientos y reglamentos. Lo hizo para crear en {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} una sola humanidad nueva a partir de los dos, haciendo así la paz, \v 16 y para reconciliar con Dios a ambos en un solo cuerpo por medio de la cruz, con la cual dio muerte a la enemistad.
es.R: {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} mismo es nuestra paz. Ha unido a los judíos y a los que no son judíos en un solo pueblo. Entre ellos había un muro, y eran como enemigos. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} derribó ese muro cuando murió en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio cuerpo. \v 15 Quitó a la ley, con todos sus mandatos y reglas, el poder de mantenerlos separados. Lo hizo para formar con los dos grupos un solo pueblo nuevo, unido a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}}. Así hizo la paz. \v 16 Por medio de la cruz llevó a los dos grupos a Dios como un solo cuerpo, en paz con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. En la cruz puso fin a la enemistad.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ndiye amani yetu, aliyevifanya vyote viwili kuwa kimoja na kuubomoa ukuta wa kati wa kizuizi, uadui, katika mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, \v 15 akiwa ameibatilisha sheria ya amri katika kanuni, ili awaumbe hao wawili ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kuwa binadamu mmoja mpya, akifanya amani, \v 16 na kuwapatanisha hao wote wawili na Mungu, wakiwa mwili mmoja, kupitia msalaba, akiwa ameufisha uadui kwa msalaba huo;
sw.B: Kwa maana {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ndiye amani yetu. Ameyafanya makundi hayo mawili kuwa moja, na ameubomoa ukuta uliowatenganisha, yaani uadui uliokuwa kati yao. Katika mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe \v 15 aliiondolea nguvu sheria pamoja na amri zake na kanuni zake. Alifanya hivyo ili ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aumbe jamii moja mpya ya wanadamu kutoka kwa wale wawili, na hivyo akaleta amani, \v 16 na ili kupitia msalaba awapatanishe na Mungu wote wawili, wakiwa mwili mmoja; kwa msalaba huo aliufisha uadui.
sw.R: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ndiye amani yetu. Amewafanya Wayahudi na watu wasio Wayahudi kuwa jamii moja. Kulikuwa na ukuta kati yao, nao walikuwa kama maadui. Lakini aliubomoa ukuta huo alipokufa katika mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe. \v 15 Aliiondolea sheria, pamoja na amri zake zote na kanuni zake, nguvu ya kuwatenganisha. Alifanya hivyo ili makundi hayo mawili yawe jamii moja mpya, iliyounganishwa naye. Kwa njia hiyo alileta amani. \v 16 Kupitia msalaba aliyaleta makundi yote mawili kwa Mungu kama mwili mmoja, yakiwa na amani naye. Msalabani alikomesha uadui.

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} notre paix, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui des deux a fait un et a abattu le mur de séparation de la clôture, l’inimitié, dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} chair, \v 15 ayant rendu sans effet la Loi des commandements [exprimés] en prescriptions, afin de créer en {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} les deux en un seul {{gender:être humain nouveau|homme nouveau}}, en faisant la paix, \v 16 et de réconcilier les uns et les autres en un seul corps avec Dieu par la croix, ayant tué par elle l’inimitié ;
fr.B: Car le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} notre paix. Des deux groupes, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait un seul, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a abattu le mur qui les séparait, l’hostilité qui les opposait. Dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre corps, \v 15 {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rendu sans effet la Loi, avec ses commandements et ses prescriptions. Il l’a fait pour créer en {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, à partir des deux, une seule humanité nouvelle, en établissant ainsi la paix, \v 16 et pour les réconcilier tous les deux avec Dieu en un seul corps par la croix, par laquelle {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a mis à mort l’hostilité.
fr.R: Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} notre paix. Des Juifs et des non-Juifs, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait un seul peuple. Un mur se dressait entre eux, et ils étaient comme des ennemis. Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a abattu ce mur quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre corps. \v 15 Il a mis fin au pouvoir de la Loi, avec tous ses commandements et toutes ses règles, qui les tenait séparés. Il l’a fait pour que les deux groupes deviennent un seul peuple nouveau, uni à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. C’est ainsi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait la paix. \v 16 Par la croix, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a amené les deux groupes à Dieu, comme un seul corps, en paix avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Sur la croix, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a mis fin à l’hostilité.

decisions.choice: Christ himself is our peace: he does not only bring peace; he is the one in whom it exists
decisions.reason: αὐτὸς ("he himself") is emphatic and refers to Christ, just named in verse 13. The peace is between Jews and Gentiles (verses 14-15) and also between both and God (verse 16); verse 17 calls it good news. Isaiah calls the coming king "Prince of Peace" (Isaiah 9:6).

decisions.choice: both, the two: Jews and Gentiles
decisions.reason: τὰ ἀμφότερα ("both") is neuter at first, speaking of the two groups as two things; then Paul uses masculine forms, τοὺς δύο ("the two") and τοὺς ἀμφοτέρους ("both"), for the people themselves. Verses 11-13 have named them: the Gentiles who were far away and Israel who was near.

decisions.choice: the dividing wall: the barrier that kept Jews and Gentiles apart; it may recall the barrier in the Jerusalem temple
alternatives: a barrier between God and humanity only
decisions.reason: μεσότοιχον τοῦ φραγμοῦ is "the middle wall of the fence", a wall that divides. Verse 15 says what made it: the law, which set Israel apart. In Paul's day a low stone barrier in the Jerusalem temple kept Gentiles out of the inner courts, with notices warning that any Gentile who passed it would be put to death; Josephus describes it, and two of the warning stones have been found. Paul himself was accused of taking an Ephesian, Trophimus, past it (Acts 21:28-29). Whether Paul has that barrier in mind here is not certain; his words would fit it, but the wall he means is the separation itself.

decisions.choice: the hostility is the dividing wall, named a second way; "in his flesh" goes with abolishing the law
alternatives: "the hostility" is the object of "abolished", with the law named beside it: he abolished the hostility, the law, in his flesh
decisions.reason: τὴν ἔχθραν is in the same case as the wall and as the law, and could stand beside either. The SBLGNT sets it off with commas on both sides. Read with the wall, it says what the wall was: hostility. ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ ("in his flesh") then tells how the law was set aside: by his bodily death (Colossians 1:22). Either way Christ removed the hostility by his death and set aside the law as a dividing wall.

decisions.choice: the law of commandments in decrees: the law of Moses as a code of commands and regulations, which set Israel apart from the nations; Christ put it out of force in that role
alternatives: only the ceremonial parts of the law
only the condemnation the law brings
decisions.reason: ἐν δόγμασιν describes the law as a set of decrees, as Colossians 2:14 and 2:20 do. Paul does not divide the law into parts here; he speaks of it as a whole, as the wall between Jews and Gentiles, with commands such as circumcision, food laws and festivals that marked Israel off (Colossians 2:16). καταργήσας means to make ineffective, to put out of force. Yet in 6:2-3 Paul still quotes one of the law's commandments to guide believers, so what is ended is the law's role as the boundary of God's people, not God's will for how people should live (Romans 3:31).

decisions.choice: one new man: one new humanity, a single new people made of Jews and Gentiles together
alternatives: Gentiles brought in to become Jews
each believer made a new individual
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπον here means a human being, not a male. Christ does not make Gentiles into Jews or Jews into Gentiles; he creates something new out of both, "in himself" (Galatians 3:28; Colossians 3:10-11). The language of creation (κτίσῃ) matches verse 10.

decisions.choice: in one body: the church, the one body of Christ
alternatives: Christ's own body, given on the cross
decisions.reason: Ephesians calls the church Christ's body (1:23; 4:4), and "one" here matches "one new humanity" in verse 15. Christ's physical body was named in verse 14 ("in his flesh"), and the two ideas are close: the church is made one through his body given on the cross.

decisions.choice: reconcile to God: bring both Jews and Gentiles into peace with God
decisions.reason: ἀποκαταλλάξῃ means to restore to friendship. Here both groups, not only the Gentiles, are reconciled to God, as in Colossians 1:20-22. So the hostility in this verse includes hostility between people and God, not only between Jews and Gentiles.

decisions.choice: having killed the hostility by it: by the cross
alternatives: in himself, in his own person
decisions.reason: ἐν αὐτῷ could refer to the cross, just named, or to Christ. The SBLGNT prints αὐτῷ here, while in verse 15 it prints the reflexive αὑτῷ ("in himself"); the change suits "by it", the cross. The meaning is much the same: the hostility died when Christ died.

decisions.choice: one new {{gender:human being|man}}
decisions.reason: The word means a human being of either sex (m6); "man" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: one new humanity (B); one new people (R)
decisions.reason: "Humanity" and "people" say that a single new people is meant, made of both groups (m6), and are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Christ, since this record begins a new sentence (m1).

decisions.choice: Jews and Gentiles ... when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body ... the power of the law ... to keep them apart
decisions.reason: Readable names the two groups (m2), says what "in his flesh" refers to (m4), and says in what sense the law was set aside (m5).

decisions.choice: set aside
decisions.reason: The verb means to make ineffective or put out of force (m5); "abolished" can suggest that the law is declared wrong.

decisions.choice: brought both groups to God as one body, at peace with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
alternatives: reconciled both to God in one body
decisions.reason: Readable says what reconciling means (m8).

decisions.choice: vyote viwili ... kimoja (v. 14); hao wawili (v. 15)
decisions.reason: Paul first speaks of the two groups with a neuter, as two things, then with masculine forms for the people themselves (m2). Swahili Literal can show the same shift: class 8 "vyote viwili" and class 7 "kimoja" for things, then the personal "hao wawili" and "wote wawili". Balanced and Readable say "makundi" (groups) or name Jews and Gentiles.

decisions.choice: binadamu mmoja mpya (L); jamii moja mpya ya wanadamu (B); jamii moja mpya (R); no gender setting
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπον is a human being, not a male (m6), and "binadamu" already includes men and women, so there is no gender span where the English Literal has one. "Ubinadamu" usually means human nature or humaneness, so Balanced says "jamii ... ya wanadamu" (a community of human beings) for the one new people. For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: un seul {{gender:être humain nouveau|homme nouveau}} (L); une seule humanité nouvelle (B); un seul peuple nouveau (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a human being of either sex (m6). As in Colossians 3:10, "l’homme nouveau" stays as the traditional alternative; Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: rendu sans effet (L, B); mis fin au pouvoir (R); la Loi, with a capital
decisions.reason: The verb means to put out of force (m5); "abolir" could suggest that the Law was declared wrong. The capital marks the Law of Moses, as the style guide sets out.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν εὐηγγελίσατο εἰρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς μακρὰν καὶ εἰρήνην τοῖς ἐγγύς·

records.literal_gloss: And having come he proclaimed good news, peace to you the [ones] far off and peace to the [ones] near;

en.L: And having come, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} proclaimed as good news peace to you who [were] far off and peace to those [who were] near;
en.B: He came with good news: peace for you who were far off, and peace for those who were near.
en.R: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came with good news. He brought peace to you Gentiles, who were far away from God. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought peace to the Jewish people, who were near.

es.L: Y habiendo venido, anunció como buena noticia paz a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que [estaban] lejos, y paz a los que [estaban] cerca;
es.B: Vino con la buena noticia: paz para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} lejos, y paz para los que estaban cerca.
es.R: {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} vino con la buena noticia. Trajo paz a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que no son judíos, que {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} lejos de Dios. Y trajo paz al pueblo judío, que estaba cerca.

sw.L: Naye alipokuja, aliitangaza amani kuwa habari njema kwenu [mliokuwa] mbali, na amani kwa [wale waliokuwa] karibu;
sw.B: Alikuja na habari njema: amani kwenu ninyi mlio mbali, na amani kwa wale walio karibu.
sw.R: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikuja na habari njema. Aliwaletea amani ninyi watu wasio Wayahudi, mliokuwa mbali na Mungu. Na aliwaletea amani Wayahudi, waliokuwa karibu.

fr.L: Et étant venu, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a annoncé comme une bonne nouvelle la paix à vous qui [étiez] loin et la paix à ceux qui [étaient] près ;
fr.B: Il est venu annoncer la bonne nouvelle : la paix pour vous qui étiez loin, et la paix pour ceux qui étaient près.
fr.R: Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est venu avec une bonne nouvelle. Il a apporté la paix à vous, les non-Juifs, qui étiez loin de Dieu. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a apporté la paix au peuple juif, qui était près.

decisions.choice: Paul takes up Isaiah 57:19, "Peace, peace, to the far and to the near", with an echo of Isaiah 52:7
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 57:19 God promises peace to his scattered people, those far away and those near. Paul applies "far" to the Gentiles and "near" to Israel (verse 13). Isaiah says "peace, peace" together and then names the two groups; Paul gives "peace" to each group in turn, keeping the doubled word. εὐηγγελίσατο ("announced good news") recalls Isaiah 52:7, where the messenger brings good news of peace, and the Greek Old Testament there uses the same verb.

decisions.choice: having come: Christ's coming as a whole, especially his death and resurrection, after which peace was announced
alternatives: his preaching during his earthly ministry
his coming through the apostles and the Spirit
decisions.reason: The coming follows the making of peace on the cross (verse 16), so it is most naturally the risen Christ who announces it, as he greeted his disciples with "Peace to you" (John 20:19-21) and then spoke through those he sent (3:5-8). But ἐλθὼν may simply sum up his whole coming into the world.

decisions.choice: came with good news
decisions.reason: The verb means to announce good news (m1); Balanced keeps that meaning.

decisions.choice: you Gentiles, who were far away from God ... the Jewish people, who were near
alternatives: you who were far off ... those who were near
decisions.reason: Readable says who the far and the near are (m1).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ as the subject.

decisions.choice: anunció como buena noticia (L); vino con la buena noticia (B, R)
alternatives: anunció el evangelio de la paz
decisions.reason: The verb means to announce good news (m1). "Evangelizar" now suggests preaching to convert, and "evangelio" is kept for the noun, so every level says "buena noticia".

decisions.choice: habari njema, lowercase
